answer: Each identity must hold one share in a wind cooperative, one per household, ledger-recorded. The share names one member, one turbine and the oasis settlement it powers; second claims are rejected. Buying in costs 1,200 units plus 300 in fees and a 60-day metered season; 100 fakes cost 150,000 units, 100 shares and 6,000 member-days. A raven-stamped meter on each turbine is read monthly, so forged shares fail at audit. Borrowing a share is the cheapest shortcut, but the lender loses dividends and vote while lent, and even a whisper of shared voting triggers an inspection revoking both.
